claim: The latest upstream RAUC release is v1.15.2, published 2026-03-27.

Debian 13 (trixie) ships RAUC 1.13-3+deb13u1, and the D-Bus daemon is a separate package rauc-service; with only the rauc package installed, `rauc status`/`mark-good` fail with 'The name de.pengutronix.rauc was not provided by any .service files'.
source_url: http://deb.debian.org/debian/dists/trixie/ (apt-cache show rauc rauc-service; output in evidence/lab/rauc/logs/versions.txt)

claim: RAUC marks the target slot non-bootable before writing it and marks it bootable (active/primary) only after all slots are written.
RAUC's GRUB backend implements mark-good as <slot>_OK=1,<slot>_TRY=0 and mark-bad as <slot>_OK=0,<slot>_TRY=0 in grubenv.
RAUC's GRUB backend activates a slot by setting <slot>_OK=1, <slot>_TRY=0 and putting it first in ORDER.
RAUC's reference GRUB script boots the first slot in ORDER with OK=1 and TRY=0, then sets its TRY=1 before booting, so an uncommitted slot gets exactly one boot attempt.
RAUC docs say the grubenv must live outside the redundant rootfs partitions, e.g. /EFI/BOOT/grubenv on the EFI partition, with load_env/save_env --file in grub.cfg.
RAUC docs recommend a systemd service that runs `rauc status mark-good` after the relevant services have come up.

RAUC verifies the signing chain with OpenSSL purpose 'smimesign' by default; certificates with the codeSigning extended key usage need check-purpose=codesign-rauc in the keyring config (lab: RAUC 1.13 rejected a codeSigning-EKU signer with 'unsuitable certificate purpose').
Home Assistant OS's x86 GRUB script stores grubenv on the ESP and allows up to 3 boot attempts per slot (TRY<3) before falling back.
The Home Assistant Supervisor commits the booted slot by calling RAUC Mark(GOOD, 'booted') over D-Bus in its mark_healthy job, i.e. HAOS's gate is 'Supervisor is running', not 'all apps healthy'.
The lab image is Debian 13 amd64 with kernel 6.12.116+deb13-amd64 and GRUB 2.12-9+deb13u2.

Lab: on Debian 13 x86_64 + RAUC 1.13 + GRUB (UEFI) in QEMU, a signed good update installed in 60-62 s (1.8 GB ext4 image, verity bundle 239 MB, TCG emulation) and committed via a health gate; a second reboot stayed on the new slot (T3).
Lab: a bundle signed by a CA not in the keyring was refused ('unable to get local issuer certificate'), with the GRUB boot environment unchanged (T2).
Lab: an update that boots but whose core service fails was rejected by the health gate (mark-bad + reboot) and the machine returned to the previous version with no human input, within 2 boots (T4).
Lab: an update whose init exits (kernel panic 'Attempted to kill init!') rebooted via panic=5 and GRUB fell back to the previous slot with no human input (T5).
Lab: SIGKILL of QEMU at 47% of the slot write left A_OK=0 (target marked bad before the write); the next boot ran the old slot and a repeated install succeeded and committed (T6).

Lab: SIGKILL after the new slot booted but before the health gate committed it made the next boot fall back to the previous slot (T7): one interrupted first boot is enough to abandon an update with RAUC's reference one-try GRUB script.
Lab: grub-mkstandalone (GRUB 2.12, x86_64-efi) does not auto-load part_gpt; without explicit insmod the embedded config cannot see (hd0,gpt1) and GRUB drops to its shell.
